record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups
record.original_question: For a zero-dimensional topological space X, is the free topological inverse semigroup I(X) over X also zero-dimensional?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An inverse semigroup is a semigroup S in which, for every element a ∈ S, there exists a unique element a⁻¹ ∈ S (called the inverse of a) such that a·a⁻¹·a = a and a⁻¹·a·a⁻¹ = a⁻¹. A topological inverse semigroup is an inverse semigroup endowed with a Hausdorff topology making both the multiplication S × S → S and the inversion S → S, a ↦ a⁻¹, continuous.

Given a topological space X, the free topological inverse semigroup over X is a topological inverse semigroup I(X) together with a continuous map η : X → I(X) such that for every continuous map f : X → T into a topological inverse semigroup T there is a unique continuous inverse-semigroup homomorphism f̄ : I(X) → T with f̄ ∘ η = f.

Recall that a topological space is called zero-dimensional if it is a T₁ space possessing a base consisting of clopen (simultaneously closed and open) sets.

Question: If X is a zero-dimensional topological space, is the free topological inverse semigroup I(X) over X necessarily zero-dimensional?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any published resolution of the question whether zero-dimensionality of a space X transfers to the free topological inverse semigroup I(X). The problem appears in a list of open problems on topological groups and semigroups, and no subsequent paper indexed by the search clearly settles it. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: A topological approach to inverse and regular semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies topological inverse semigroups but does not address free topological inverse semigroups over zero-dimensional spaces.
status_evidence.claim: General references on topological inverse semigroups do not appear to resolve the zero-dimensionality question for I(X).

status_evidence.title: Categorically Closed Unipotent Semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on topological semigroups; does not state a resolution of the zero-dimensionality of free topological inverse semigroups.
status_evidence.claim: No recent resolution of the problem was identified.
